Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
problems.postgresql:
SELECT v.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS count_no_trans
FROM Visits v
LEFT JOIN Transactions t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id

problems.title: Rising Temperature
problems.postgresql:
SELECT today.id
FROM Weather today
JOIN Weather yesterday ON today.recordDate = yesterday.recordDate + 1
WHERE today.temperature > yesterday.temperature;

problems.title: Average Time of Process per Machine
problems.postgresql:
SELECT s.machine_id,
       ROUND(AVG(e.timestamp - s.timestamp), 3) AS processing_time
FROM Activity s
JOIN Activity e
  ON s.machine_id = e.machine_id
 AND s.process_id = e.process_id
WHERE s.activity_type = 'start'
  AND e.activity_type = 'end'
GROUP BY s.machine_id;

problems.title: Employee Bonus
problems.postgresql:
SELECT e.name, b.bonus
FROM Employee e
LEFT JOIN Bonus b ON e.empId = b.empId
WHERE b.bonus < 1000 OR b.bonus IS NULL;

problems.title: Students and Examinations
problems.postgresql:
SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, sub.subject_name,
       COUNT(e.subject_name) AS attended_exams
FROM Students s
CROSS JOIN Subjects sub
LEFT JOIN Examinations e
       ON e.student_id = s.student_id
      AND e.subject_name = sub.subject_name
GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, sub.subject_name
ORDER BY s.student_id, sub.subject_name;

problems.title: Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports
problems.postgresql:
SELECT m.name
FROM Employee m
JOIN Employee e ON e.managerId = m.id
GROUP BY m.id, m.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

problems.title: Confirmation Rate
problems.postgresql:
SELECT s.user_id,
       ROUND(COALESCE(AVG((c.action = 'confirmed')::int), 0), 2) AS confirmation_rate
FROM Signups s
LEFT JOIN Confirmations c ON s.user_id = c.user_id
GROUP BY s.user_id;

problems.title: Not Boring Movies
problems.postgresql:
SELECT *
FROM Cinema
WHERE id % 2 = 1 AND description <> 'boring'
ORDER BY rating DESC;

problems.title: Average Selling Price
problems.postgresql:
SELECT p.product_id,
       COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(p.price * u.units)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(u.units), 0), 2), 0) AS average_price
FROM Prices p
LEFT JOIN UnitsSold u
       ON p.product_id = u.product_id
      AND u.purchase_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date
GROUP BY p.product_id;

problems.title: Project Employees I
problems.postgresql:
SELECT p.project_id, ROUND(AVG(e.experience_years), 2) AS average_years
FROM Project p
JOIN Employee e ON p.employee_id = e.employee_id
GROUP BY p.project_id;

problems.title: Percentage of Users Attended a Contest
problems.postgresql:
SELECT contest_id,
       ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Users), 2) AS percentage
FROM Register
GROUP BY contest_id
ORDER BY percentage DESC, contest_id;

problems.title: Queries Quality and Percentage
problems.postgresql:
SELECT query_name,
       ROUND(AVG(rating::numeric / position), 2) AS quality,
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG((rating < 3)::int), 2) AS poor_query_percentage
FROM Queries
WHERE query_name IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY query_name;

problems.title: Monthly Transactions I
problems.postgresql:
SELECT TO_CHAR(trans_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       country,
       COUNT(*) AS trans_count,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'approved') AS approved_count,
       SUM(amount) AS trans_total_amount,
       COALESCE(SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE state = 'approved'), 0) AS approved_total_amount
FROM Transactions
GROUP BY TO_CHAR(trans_date, 'YYYY-MM'), country;

problems.title: Immediate Food Delivery II
problems.postgresql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * AVG((order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date)::int), 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery
WHERE (customer_id, order_date) IN (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date)
    FROM Delivery
    GROUP BY customer_id
);

problems.title: Game Play Analysis IV
problems.postgresql:
SELECT ROUND(COUNT(a.player_id)::numeric / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) FROM Activity), 2) AS fraction
FROM Activity a
JOIN (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date) AS first_login
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
) f ON a.player_id = f.player_id
   AND a.event_date = f.first_login + 1;

problems.title: Number of Unique Subjects Taught by Each Teacher
User Activity for the Past 30 Days I

FROM Activity

problems.title: Product Sales Analysis III
problems.postgresql:

FROM Sales
WHERE (product_id, year) IN (
    SELECT product_id, MIN(year)
    FROM Sales

problems.title: The Number of Employees Which Report to Each Employee
problems.postgresql:
SELECT m.employee_id, m.name,
       COUNT(*) AS reports_count,
       ROUND(AVG(e.age)) AS average_age
FROM Employees e
JOIN Employees m ON e.reports_to = m.employee_id
GROUP BY m.employee_id, m.name
ORDER BY m.employee_id;

FROM Employee

   OR employee_id IN (

        FROM Employee

problems.title: Triangle Judgement
Consecutive Numbers
problems.postgresql:
SELECT DISTINCT l1.num AS "ConsecutiveNums"
FROM Logs l1
JOIN Logs l2 ON l2.id = l1.id + 1 AND l2.num = l1.num
JOIN Logs l3 ON l3.id = l1.id + 2 AND l3.num = l1.num;

problems.title: Product Price at a Given Date
problems.postgresql:
SELECT p.product_id, COALESCE(l.new_price, 10) AS price
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM Products) p
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (product_id) product_id, new_price
    FROM Products
    WHERE change_date <= DATE '2019-08-16'
    ORDER BY product_id, change_date DESC
) l ON p.product_id = l.product_id;

problems.title: Last Person to Fit in the Bus
problems.postgresql:
SELECT person_name
FROM (
    SELECT person_name, SUM(weight) OVER (ORDER BY turn) AS total_weight
    FROM Queue
) t
WHERE total_weight <= 1000
ORDER BY total_weight DESC
LIMIT 1;

problems.title: Count Salary Categories
problems.postgresql:
SELECT 'Low Salary' AS category,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE income < 20000) AS accounts_count
FROM Accounts
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Average Salary',
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE income BETWEEN 20000 AND 50000)
FROM Accounts
UNION ALL
SELECT 'High Salary',
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE income > 50000)
FROM Accounts;

problems.title: Exchange Seats
problems.postgresql:
SELECT CASE
           WHEN id % 2 = 1 AND id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM Seat) THEN id
           WHEN id % 2 = 1 THEN id + 1
           ELSE id - 1
       END AS id,
       student
FROM Seat
ORDER BY id;

problems.title: Movie Rating
problems.postgresql:
(SELECT u.name AS results
 FROM MovieRating r
 JOIN Users u ON r.user_id = u.user_id
 GROUP BY u.user_id, u.name
 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, u.name
 LIMIT 1)
UNION ALL

problems.title: Restaurant Growth
problems.postgresql:
WITH daily AS (
    SELECT visited_on, SUM(amount) AS amount
    FROM Customer
    GROUP BY visited_on
)
SELECT visited_on, amount, average_amount
FROM (
    SELECT visited_on,
           SUM(amount) OVER w AS amount,
           ROUND(AVG(amount) OVER w, 2) AS average_amount
    FROM daily
    WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY visited_on RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '6 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
) t
WHERE visited_on >= (SELECT MIN(visited_on) FROM daily) + 6
ORDER BY visited_on;

problems.title: Friend Requests II: Who Has the Most Friends
problems.postgresql:
SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS num
FROM (
    SELECT requester_id AS id FROM RequestAccepted
    UNION ALL
    SELECT accepter_id FROM RequestAccepted
) t
GROUP BY id
ORDER BY num DESC
LIMIT 1;

problems.title: Investments in 2016
problems.postgresql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(tiv_2016)::numeric, 2) AS tiv_2016
FROM (
    SELECT tiv_2016,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY tiv_2015) AS same_2015,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY lat, lon) AS same_location
    FROM Insurance
) t
WHERE same_2015 > 1 AND same_location = 1;

problems.title: Department Top Three Salaries
problems.postgresql:
SELECT d.name AS "Department", e.name AS "Employee", e.salary AS "Salary"
FROM (
    SELECT name, salary, departmentId,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY departmentId ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk
    FROM Employee
) e
JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
WHERE e.rnk <= 3;

problems.title: Fix Names in a Table
problems.postgresql:
SELECT user_id,
       UPPER(LEFT(name, 1)) || LOWER(SUBSTRING(name FROM 2)) AS name
FROM Users
ORDER BY user_id;

problems.title: List the Products Ordered in a Period
problems.postgresql:
SELECT p.product_name, SUM(o.unit) AS unit
FROM Products p
JOIN Orders o ON p.product_id = o.product_id
WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2020-02-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2020-03-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING SUM(o.unit) >= 100;
